Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE3708 : Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machines Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Module 1 :

1. Verification of Bernoulli’s theory.
2. Determination of coefficient of discharge for V-notch.
3. Determination of coefficient of discharge for Rectangular notch.
4. Determination of coefficient of discharge for Orifice meter.
5. Determination of coefficient of discharge for Venturimeter.

Understand the concept of fluid mechanics and hydraulic machines.

Demonstrate the experiments in fluid mechanics and hydraulic machinery.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6532 : Modeling and Simulation of Bioprocesses { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Basic Modelling Principles (8 Contact Hours)
Introduction , definition of modelling and simulation, different types of models, Mass transfer: liquid - liquid, liquid - gas, liquid - solid mass transfer, Stoichiometry
Module 2: Mathematical Models for Biochemical Engineering Systems (10 Contact Hours)
Batch Reactor, CSTR, Fed Batch reactor, Batch Distillation, Isothermal with cooling/heating jacket or coil
Module 3: Modelling of Bioprocesses (6 Contact Hours)
Modelling approaches for Biological Systems Growth Kinetic Models- Structured and unstructured, Compartmental models, deterministic and stochastic approaches, death kinetic models.
Module 4: Numerical Methods and Analysis(5 contact Hours):
Rungge Kutta and Newton Raphson, Stability Analysis, basic data analysis-curve fitting, sensitivity analysis.
Module 5: Case Studies (7 Contact Hours)
Model for: lactic acid fermentation, antibiotic production, ethanol fermentation, activated sludge processes, Anaerobic digestion

Course Objective

1 .

Students will be able to develop mathematical models of bioprocesses using mass and heat conservation principles
2 .

The students will be able to identify system boundaries and relate the governing variables through a methodological approach.
3 .

The students will be able to integrate a differential algebraic system for bioprocess using MATLAB.
4 .

Acquire proficiency in recruiting numerical methods for solving models based on difference equations for a particular use case

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students would be able to gain understanding of different types of models and methodology generally recruited for bioprocess engineering.
2. The students will be able to develop mathematical models for various bioprocesses with the help of first principles.
3. Students will be able to identify and define a system, state variables and processes of a given bioprocess.
4. The students will be able to understand the principles of solving difference equation based mathematical models.
5. Students will be able to simulate a bioprocess on MATLAB.

J.E. Bailey and D.F. Ollis, Biochemical Engg Fundamentals, McGraw Hill

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ER5504 : Boundary Layer Meteorology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1
What is atmospheric boundary layer? Atmospheric turbulence, Boussinesq approximation, Reynolds equations, Dispersion and its behaviour in boundary layer, Reynolds number, Rayleigh number and Richardson number, Friction velocity, Free convection scaling variables, Reynold’s decomposition and averaging, Taylor’s hypothesis, Eddy covariance method, average, variance, standard deviation and covariance in micrometeorology, Eddy heat flux concept.
Module 2
Simplifications and approximations, Mean boundary layer characteristics, Equations for mean variables in a turbulent flow, Prognostic equations for turbulent departures and mean variables, Bosinessq approximation, Shallow motion and shallow convection approximations, Prognostic equations for fluxes and variances.
Module 3
TKE budget equation, Turbulent closure techniques, Mixed layer theory, Momentum equations for PBL – Well mixed boundary layer, The flux – gradient theory, Mixing length theory, Ekman layer, Surface layer, Modified Ekman layer, Turbulence Closure Techniques, Similarity Theory, Stable boundary layer, Modeling and evolution of stable boundary layer over land surface.
Module 4
Urban boundary layer characteristics, Urban heat island, Urban modification of flow, Urban weather and mesoscale weather, Atmospheric boundary layer modeling and parameterizations, Surface Radiation budget and Surface Heat budget, Atmospheric Pollution: Type of pollutants, gaseous and particulate pollutants, Urban Air Pollution, Boundary conditions and external forcings Similarity theory Convective mixed layer Stable boundary layer Boundary layer clouds.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce the fundamentals of atmospheric boundary layer, turbulence in the atmosphere and resulting complexities.
2 .

Developing an understanding about various simplifications applicable for solutions in the boundary layer, and how pollution dispersion is governed by the boundary layer principles.
3 .

To understand the conversion of mass, momentum, energy principles application by considering turbulence in the atmospheric boundary layer.
4 .

4. Exploring the modification of boundary layer concepts with urbanization.
5. Developing basic understanding of air pollution and role of boundary layer in its transformation.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: To describe and explain the salient features of turbulent boundary layers in atmosphere.
CO2: To examine and investigate the derivation and applications of conservation of mass, momentum, energy in the atmospheric boundary layer with the limitations, approximations, and assumptions for solving the equations in a real-world scenario.
CO3: To explain, and categorize the spectral evolution of turbulence, and the dominant terms of the budget equations for turbulence in the atmosphere and to develop knowledge on sources and sink mechanisms driving turbulence in atmosphere.
CO4: To understand the pollution transport and dispersion mechanism as per atmospheric boundary layer principles with its application to practical situations.
CO5: To analyze and explain different surface energy budget conditions, similarity theory for formulation of dimensionless relations between variables in the boundary layer.

Essential Reading

1 .

Roland B. Stull, An introduction to boundary layer meteorology, Kluwer Academic Publishers , 1988

2 .

S. Pal Arya, Introduction to Micrometeorology, Academic Press , 2001

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Roland B. Stull, Meteorology for scientists and Engineers, Brooks/Cole Thomson Learning , 2000

2 .

Foken, T. and Napo, C.J., Micrometeorology, Springer , 2008

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME3301 : Heat Transfer { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1 [2 hours] (Introduction): Modes of heat transfer Combined heat transfer mechanism Analogy between the flows of heat and electricity.
Module 2 [14 hours] (Conduction): Fourier law of heat conduction for isotropic material Thermal conductivity Three-dimensional Fourier conduction equation in cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinate systems Derivation of general heat conduction equation Thermal diffusivity Types of boundary conditions Solution of steady one-dimensional conduction problem with and without heat generation One-dimensional steady conduction through slab, cylinder, sphere, and composite medium Analogy with electrical circuits Critical insulation thickness Heat transfer through rectangular and pin fins Fin effectiveness and fin efficiency Fin arrangement Transient conduction without spatial effect Lumped capacitance method Fourier number Significance of time constant Biot number.
Module 3 [10 hours] (Radiation): Physical mechanism of thermal radiation Stefan-Boltzmann law, Grey body Kirchoff’s law, Wien’s displacement law) Concept of the black body, emissive power, radiation intensity, reflectivity, transmissivity, irradiation, radiosity Radiation exchange between black bodies Shape factors Concept of grey-diffuse-isotropic (GDI) surface Radiation exchange between GDI surfaces Electrical network method for solving radiation problems (by radiation network) Radiation shielding.
Module 4 [10 hours] (Convection): Velocity and thermal boundary layers for laminar flow over a flat plate Governing equations for the boundary layer over a flat plate Boundary layer approximations Solution of boundary layer equations for laminar flow over a flat plate by integral method External laminar and turbulent flow over an isothermal plate Mixed boundary layer over an isothermal plate Heat transfer for laminar flow in circular tubes/pipes with constant surface heat flux and constant surface temperature conditions Concept of developing and developed flow Concept of log mean temperature difference, average heat transfer coefficient Turbulent flow in circular tubes One-dimensional solution for Couette and Poiseulli flow.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce the fundamentals of heat transfer and help to develop methodologies for solving various real-life engineering problems involving heat transfer.
2 .

To learn about the conduction mode of heat transfer and the process of analyzing the problem involving conduction heat transfer.
3 .

To learn the types of heat convection, the physics behind convection heat transfer, and how to analyze the convection heat transfer.
4 .

To learn different laws of radiation, the way of radiation heat transfer, and the method of analyzing the real-life phenomena involving radiation heat transfer.

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of this course, the students will be able
CO1: To understand the fundamental principles and mathematical basis underlying the balance equations for heat transfer and solve practical engineering problems using basic concepts of heat and mass transfer.
CO2: To grasp the principles and mechanisms of heat conduction and develop a comprehensive understanding of its applications, to apply transient conduction concepts using lumped capacitance and similarity transformation methods
CO3: To develop a deep understanding of convective heat transfer and provide design solutions by handling governing equations for both laminar flow and natural convection and to capture the development of momentum and thermal boundary layers in laminar flows
CO4: To determine radiation heat transfer rates in real-life phenomena involving radiation heat transfer by analyzing different laws of radiation and ways of radiation heat transfer
CO5: To perform design calculations of thermal equipment and solve real-life engineering problems involved with different modes of heat transfer like heat transfer enhancement through extended surfaces, lumped heat capacity systems, heat exchangers, heat interaction of the flow through pipes, etc.

Essential Reading

Frank P. Incropera, David P. Dewitt, Theodore L. Bergman, Adrienne S. Lavine, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, John Wiley & Sons , 8th Edition Reprint

2 .

Yunus A. Çengel, Afshin J. Ghajar, Heat and Mass Transfer: Fundamentals and Applications, McGraw Hill , 6th Edition Reprint
